subject: general
question: What is reverberation?

options.text: Spreading of sound in all directions
Persistence of sound due to multiple reflections of sound waves
Loss of sound energy in air

solution:
The correct answer is __**Persistence of sound due to multiple reflections of sound waves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Reverberation** is defined as the **persistence of sound** in a particular space after the original sound source has stopped. It occurs because sound waves undergo **multiple reflections** from surfaces such as **walls, ceilings, and floors** in an enclosed area.
 
• In a large room or auditorium, a sound created will continue to be heard by **repeated reflection** until its intensity is reduced to a level where it is no longer audible.
 
• The human ear has a **persistence of hearing** of approximately **0.1 seconds**. When reflected sound waves arrive at the ear in intervals shorter than this, the brain perceives them as a single, continuous, and prolonged sound rather than distinct echoes. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
